strategy: Synthetic-base three-way merge: preserve the exact Orange Pi vendor tree as ours, use Android common immediately after its upstream Linux 5.4.125 merge as the base, and merge Android common 5.4.302 as theirs. The target contains upstream v5.4.302 and the maintained Android 12 5.4 patch set.

semantic_merge_required.drivers/char/Kconfig: Use the maintained 5.4.302 RNG/Kconfig text and retain the seven vendor SUNXI character-driver Kconfig inclusions.
semantic_merge_required.drivers/cpufreq/sun50i-cpufreq-nvmem.c: Preserve the complete sun50iw9/sun50iw10 efuse/bin implementation and carry the stable allocation cleanup into vendor error paths.
semantic_merge_required.drivers/pinctrl/sunxi/pinctrl-sunxi.c: Preserve the complete Allwinner hardware-type, power-source, regulator and secure-pin implementation; carry only the applicable stable krealloc failure fix. The vanilla pin-base rewrite is not transplanted because the vendor implementation computes bank and hardware offsets differently.

notes: The mechanical post-merge patch removes three EOF blank lines and fixes three space-before-tab indentation instances across three non-conflict Android-common files; it changes no executable semantics and makes the pinned merged diff whitespace-clean.
The GKI ABI/build files are intentionally absent from the retained vendor tree and are not used by its validated O= make flow; their deletion is preserved.
The vendor sunxi-mmc.c is a complete Allwinner controller implementation rather than a small patch to the upstream driver, so unrelated upstream-driver fixes are not mechanically mixed into it.
Generic Android binder, FunctionFS/accessory, dm-verity, WireGuard, F2FS, pstore and networking conflicts use the maintained Android-common 5.4.302 implementations instead of older fork snapshots.
